description:
User approved version 3 of /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-nml-29-private-append.html, verbatim "agreed. this is a good place to start." (in JSON's session, relayed by JSON and Optimize, 2026-11-19). Step 2b; lands with step 2, ahead of fz-nml.28's measurement. Builder: Optimize. Agreed with Binary Handling: this is the share step; fz-9e2.6 keeps only the self-tail-call back edge.
Prim::Share and the container store (stored_form / share_if_struct -> share_if_published_kind) lower to an inline store of the mark: a store for a value typed as a mark-holding kind, nothing for one that holds no mark (integer, float, atom), a kind branch for any. Generated code no longer calls fz_mark_published_ref_aliased; the function stays for the interpreter.
Acceptance: a native-dump test that a share of a binary-typed, an integer-typed and an any-typed value emits a store, nothing, and a kind branch; the two probe loops from the page at or under 30 and 40 instructions per iteration (112 and 301 today), judged on bench; every ownership fixture unchanged on all three paths. Also removes most of the 252 instructions per iteration (mark_published_ref_aliased 150 + share 102) measured in the map case probe.

comments.text: PR #796 stacked on #789. Bench release probes, instr/iter: one binary passed twice 139→22 (target ≤30); tuple of three binaries passed twice 385→35 (target ≤40). share_class reads the type; IR shares each distinct variable once per call/tuple/closure; generated code no longer calls fz_mark_published_ref_aliased. Matrix 3914/0; 01309/01711/01712 and retention pins unmoved.

title: A share is one store in generated code, and nothing for a value that holds no mark
